market_question: Will the No to ten million Switzerland initiative be approved in Switzerland’s June 14, 2026 popular vote?
reasoning: Swiss popular initiatives rarely pass (historical ~10% success rate). The 'No to ten million Switzerland' initiative mirrors previously rejected proposals like the 2014 Ecopop (74% No) and the 2020 Limitation Initiative (62% No). The double‑majority requirement (popular plus cantonal) further reduces the chance of approval, making the market's 33.5% implied probability excessively optimistic.
evidence_points: Only ~10% of Swiss popular initiatives have ever been approved since 1891.
The 2014 Ecopop population‑cap initiative was rejected with 74% No; the 2020 Limitation Initiative was rejected with 61.7% No.
The Federal Council and Parliament recommend a 'No' vote, a situation from which few initiatives recover.
A double majority (voters and cantons) is required, lowering the likelihood even if popular support is close.
sources_consulted: Swiss Federal Chancellery historical referendum statistics
